# Agentic Catalog

> A curated, rated catalog of rules, skills, workflows, hooks, subagents, MCP servers, plugins, and user-facing developer tools for coding agents, focused on Claude Code and Codex. Every entry records where it came from, its license, tags, and a curator rating.

Full metadata for every entry is in [catalog/index.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/catalog/index.json). Install steps by entry type are in the [install guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/skills/agentic-catalog/references/install.md). Repository: https://github.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog

Human-focused rubric (human-v1): seven 0–4 grades weighted by practical value 25%, dependability 20%, cognitive ease 15%, human control 15%, adoption cost 10%, compatibility 10%, upkeep 5%; weighted total / 40 gives a score out of 10. Higher is better on every axis. Missing grades produce no aggregate. Legacy-v1 scores remain out of 5 and are not comparable. See the [rating guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/docs/ratings.md). Entries within sections are grouped: complete human-v1, legacy-v1, incomplete human-v1, then human-v1 with blockers; scores rank only within groups. Evidence: reviewed, used, tested, evaluated; inspect its actual scope. Hosts: any means an open format. Select for project fit first. Show the score scale, rubric, evidence, source and blockers before installation; never let a high average clear a blocker.

## Skills

- [Prepare and analyze moderated usability studies](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/skills/moderated-usability-study/SKILL.md): Creates realistic task scenarios, participant criteria, moderator guides and observation records, or synthesizes actual session evidence. Separates study preparation and inspection hypotheses from findings about real participants. Use when: Preparing a study with real participants or analyzing its session records, especially when comprehension, findability or task behavior is unresolved. — id `moderated-usability-study`, 8.6/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags ux, user-research, usability, study-planning, adapted from https://github.com/JoaoMonteiro100/ux-design-skills/blob/ef9596b06350cb6362716ac3acc6ea82681550ef/skills/ux-usability-study/SKILL.md, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/skills/moderated-usability-study/entry.yaml)
- [Bun monorepo workspaces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/skills/bun-workspaces/SKILL.md): Configure Bun workspace membership, dependency ownership, catalogs, linker policy and filtered task execution. Verify package resolution from the consumer scope, prerequisite ordering, frozen installation and packed public artifacts. Use when: Creating, configuring or debugging a Bun monorepo with cross-package dependency, filter, linker, catalog or package-export problems. — id `bun-workspaces`, 8.5/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags bun, monorepo, workspaces, dependencies, package-management, build-systems, testing, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/skills/bun-workspaces/entry.yaml)
- [Reviewable commit history](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/skills/commit-history-hygiene/SKILL.md): Plans a series of self-contained commits, splits mixed edits without interactive staging, writes why-focused messages in the long-standing Git style when the repository has no convention, verifies every commit with rebase --exec, folds review fixes in with fixup commits and non-interactive autosquash, and handles trailers and signing without overreach. Use when: Committing a body of work as several commits, tidying a branch before review, squashing fixups, or adding co-author or sign-off trailers. — id `commit-history-hygiene`, 8.5/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags commits, git, code-review, conventions, adapted from https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin/blob/c27add907c3a4e59713075e76049a8b0c8b4ec01/skills/ce-commit/SKILL.md, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/skills/commit-history-hygiene/entry.yaml)
- [Secret serialization review (Sentry)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/skills/secret-serialization/SKILL.md): An opt-in review for credentials that leak through generated serialization. It pairs a holder (a secret field on a dataclass, pydantic model, or JavaScript object) with a sink (logs, spans, error context, caches, or responses that serialize whole objects), searches the whole repository for the missing side, and grades each finding by the path that is still unblocked. Use when: A change adds a credential field to a dataclass, model, or config object, or adds code that stringifies whole objects or every kwarg into logs or telemetry, in Python or JavaScript and TypeScript. — id `secret-serialization`, 8.5/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags security, secrets, logging, telemetry, code-review, python, typescript, vendored from https://github.com/getsentry/skills/tree/473d2594cd91c96ac8348f297e016b631e842487/skills/secret-serialization, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/skills/secret-serialization/entry.yaml)
- [Tokio async correctness](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/skills/tokio-async-correctness/SKILL.md): Trace task ownership, partial progress, capacity and shutdown through Tokio flows. Distinguish cancellation data loss from fairness loss, detached handles from aborting task sets, and application errors from join errors. Includes a bounded intake/drain example. Use when: Reviewing or fixing Tokio select loops, lost work, orphan tasks, closed-channel spins, unbounded spawning or shutdown behavior. — id `tokio-async-correctness`, 8.5/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags rust, tokio, async, concurrency, cancellation, backpressure, testing, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/skills/tokio-async-correctness/entry.yaml)

It uses MaybeRefOrGetter for read-only inputs and MaybeRef for writable ones, normalizes with toRef() for watch sources and toValue() for one-off reads, and warns against typing callback parameters as getters, where they would be invoked by mistake. Includes secret redaction and a performance branch. ## Rules

- [Accessible Markdown documentation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/rules/markdown-accessibility/RULE.md): Keep Markdown documentation usable through meaningful links, context-appropriate image alternatives, navigable headings, semantic lists and tables, and instructions that do not depend on visual cues. Preserves decorative images, generated titles, and the project's voice and renderer conventions. Use when: Writing or reviewing Markdown documentation where screen-reader navigation, image alternatives, or visual-only instructions need attention beyond formatter and lint checks. — id `markdown-accessibility`, 8.3/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags accessibility, markdown, documentation, code-review, adapted from https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/e2c948023120a8318645170132b839280b50557e/instructions/markdown-accessibility.instructions.md, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/rules/markdown-accessibility/entry.yaml)
- [Verify in the running app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/rules/verification-evidence/RULE.md): Check a change where its effect appears, including in an app the user already has running, even when the agent may not start a server; otherwise name what remains unchecked. Use when: Agents in your project hand back visible UI changes without looking at them. — id `verification-evidence`, 8.0/10 (human-v1), evidence used, hosts any, tags dev-ux, verification, browser, completion-claims, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/rules/verification-evidence/entry.yaml)
- [Focused changes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/rules/focused-changes/RULE.md): Make the smallest coherent change that satisfies the request, follow existing project patterns, and avoid unrelated cleanup or new dependencies without a concrete need. Use when: Agents in your project tend to over-reach with refactors, new dependencies, or drive-by cleanup. — id `focused-changes`, 7.3/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags scope, diff-size, conventions, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/rules/focused-changes/entry.yaml)
- [Scope and authority](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/rules/scope-and-authority/RULE.md): Work toward the requested outcome within the authorization already given, preserve unrelated work, and ask only when the answer changes the result or more authorization is needed. Use when: You want an explicit, host-neutral statement of authorization boundaries in AGENTS.md. — id `scope-and-authority`, 7.3/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags scope, authorization, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/rules/scope-and-authority/entry.yaml)
- [Karpathy-style coding guidelines](https://github.com/multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills/blob/8462496b34419f20b32778610571ac723e91f94c/CLAUDE.md): A widely shared CLAUDE.md with four principles drawn from Andrej Karpathy's observations of LLM coding failures. Surface assumptions, write minimal code, make surgical diffs, and execute toward a goal with verification steps. Use when: You want a recognized, drop-in baseline against over-engineering and drive-by edits. — id `karpathy-coding-guidelines`, 6.9/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags scope, diff-size, simplicity, assumptions, linked from https://github.com/multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills/blob/8462496b34419f20b32778610571ac723e91f94c/CLAUDE.md, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/rules/karpathy-coding-guidelines/entry.yaml)

## Workflows and loops

- [Bun migration and verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/bun-migration-verification/WORKFLOW.md): Select package-manager, runtime, bundler and test-runner changes independently. Preserve lockfile inputs and local work, review lifecycle trust, verify clean installation and target behavior, and report scoped evidence with a recoverable rollback. Use when: Initializing a Bun project or planning, implementing or reviewing a migration to Bun package management, runtime, bundling or testing. — id `bun-migration-verification`, 8.5/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags bun, javascript, typescript, migration, package-management, verification, testing, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/bun-migration-verification/entry.yaml)
- [Monorepo change verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/monorepo-change-verification/WORKFLOW.md): Map package, task and release graphs; verify package boundaries and affected consumers; and check prerequisite ordering, cache restoration and invalidation without replacing existing monorepo tooling. Use when: Planning or verifying cross-package changes, shared build configuration, affected-task selection or package boundaries in a monorepo. — id `monorepo-change-verification`, 8.5/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags monorepo, architecture, dependencies, build-systems, caching, verification, testing, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/monorepo-change-verification/entry.yaml)
- [Rust verification ladder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/rust-verification-ladder/WORKFLOW.md): Match a Rust change to appropriate evidence, starting with existing Cargo checks and selectively using Miri, Loom, fuzzing, Kani, mutation testing or API compatibility checks. Record versions, target/features, bounds and limitations instead of treating one passing run as a proof. Use when: Choosing or reviewing verification for a Rust change involving unsafe code, concurrency, input handling, test quality or a public library API. — id `rust-verification-ladder`, 8.5/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags rust, verification, testing, unsafe-code, concurrency, fuzzing, api-compatibility, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/rust-verification-ladder/entry.yaml)
- [Harness experiment loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/harness-experiment-loop/WORKFLOW.md): Test changes to agent instructions, skills or helpers on repeatable tasks. Preserve an unchanged baseline, probe focused alternatives, compare execution evidence, rerun a selective composition and retain only supported lessons, with transfer checked separately. Use when: Deciding whether a change to agent guidance addresses an observed recurring failure before making that guidance persistent. — id `harness-experiment-loop`, 8.4/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags self-improvement, evaluation, project-instructions, skill-authoring, verification, adapted from https://github.com/google-research/harness2/blob/1cfe254e8d25b15f37048c3730134686abe60335/harness2/core/prompts.py, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/harness-experiment-loop/entry.yaml)
- [Evidence-to-flow UX decision workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/evidence-to-flow-ux/WORKFLOW.md): Connects a bounded product decision to task inspection, existing research or participant-study preparation, then a supported design change and proportionate retest. Keeps observations, hypotheses and human evidence distinct without requiring every stage. Use when: Moving from a concrete task problem or research uncertainty to a design decision, authorized change and a retest that matches the claim. — id `evidence-to-flow-ux`, 8.0/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags ux, user-research, usability, interaction-design, verification, adapted from https://github.com/ghaida/intent/blob/7111cb85894feaeb7e98938b1ed34597d40e3b4c/skills/intent/SKILL.md, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/evidence-to-flow-ux/entry.yaml)
- [Evidence-backed game balance analysis](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/game-balance-review/WORKFLOW.md): Reviews combat, economy, progression and loot against explicit rules, targets and available evidence. Separates missing inputs, structural defects, uncertain acquisition distributions and observed player outcomes. Use when: Assessing game balance from formulas, content data, progression requirements, loot rules or telemetry, and proposing bounded tuning experiments. — id `game-balance-review`, 8.0/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags game-design, balance, virtual-economies, progression, adapted from https://github.com/Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios/blob/05ad7c8a5b8aa2aa86bbd3439ae7cf7295cac418/.claude/skills/balance-check/SKILL.md, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/game-balance-review/entry.yaml)
- [Playable mechanic experiments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/mechanic-prototyping/WORKFLOW.md): Turns one gameplay uncertainty into a scoped playable experiment and an evidence-backed keep, revise, stop or inconclusive decision. Preserves the target experience and separates prototypes from production commitments. Use when: Testing a gameplay idea, control interaction or small loop before committing to production, or comparing mechanic variants in a playable prototype. — id `mechanic-prototyping`, 8.0/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags game-design, prototyping, experimentation, adapted from https://github.com/gamedev-skills/awesome-gamedev-agent-skills/blob/19d93f97c9c1ea0f8b306e77aa81e0d3e352d3e9/skills/workflows/prototype-fast/SKILL.md, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/mechanic-prototyping/entry.yaml)
- [Gameplay studies and observation workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/gameplay-playtesting/WORKFLOW.md): Prepares and interprets focused gameplay tests, keeping implementation checks, design inspection and real-player evidence separate. Connects traceable observations to decisions and comparable retests without a studio runtime. Use when: Planning gameplay studies, analyzing playtest notes or recordings, or exercising a playable build to investigate controls, learning, fairness, pacing or cooperation. — id `gameplay-playtesting`, 7.8/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags game-design, playtesting, user-research, verification, adapted from https://github.com/bmad-code-org/bmad-module-game-dev-studio/blob/ff8870955203e1665f4bf75a64049078e6d4080c/src/workflows/gametest/gds-playtest-plan/SKILL.md, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/gameplay-playtesting/entry.yaml)
- [Revise CLAUDE.md with session learnings](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/blob/a86e34672c44fa1fb1ae2b2c4143abcf26612ace/plugins/claude-md-management/commands/revise-claude-md.md): An official end-of-session command. It reflects on the context the agent lacked (commands, patterns, gotchas), picks the right CLAUDE.md, drafts one-line additions as diffs with a reason for each, and applies only the ones you approve. Use when: A session showed context the agent was missing, and you want a lightweight, approval-gated write-back to project instructions. — id `revise-claude-md`, 7.3/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts claude-code, tags self-improvement, project-instructions, memory, retrospective, linked from https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/blob/a86e34672c44fa1fb1ae2b2c4143abcf26612ace/plugins/claude-md-management/commands/revise-claude-md.md, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/revise-claude-md/entry.yaml)
- [Self-improvement loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/self-improvement-loop/WORKFLOW.md): Capture what slowed a session down, place each lesson where it will take effect (hook, always-loaded line, skill, or script), check that it loads, and prune always-loaded instructions regularly. It composes the retrospective, hook, and AGENTS.md entries in this catalog. Use when: You want the agent to learn from each session and write the lessons back into the project without bloating its instructions. — id `self-improvement-loop`, 7.0/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags self-improvement, retrospective, project-instructions, memory, context, original, informed by https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/self-improvement-loop/entry.yaml)
- [Explore, plan, implement, review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/explore-plan-implement-review/WORKFLOW.md): Explore read-only and write a plan with a check for each step before editing. Implement against the plan, then have a fresh-context reviewer compare the diff with the plan and report only gaps in correctness or requirements. Use when: A change spans several files, the approach is uncertain, or the agent will run long enough unattended that it should not grade its own work. — id `explore-plan-implement-review`, 6.4/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags planning, code-review, verification, subagents, adapted from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/explore-plan-implement-review/entry.yaml)
- [Ralph loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/ralph-loop/WORKFLOW.md): Fresh-context iteration against a plan. A shell loop reruns one fixed prompt; each pass picks one task from IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, implements it behind tests, commits, and updates the plan, until a completion token or an iteration cap. Use when: You have clear specs and a strong test suite and want long, unattended greenfield or backlog work in a sandbox. — id `ralph-loop`, 5.8/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags autonomous-loop, long-running, planning, backpressure, adapted from https://github.com/ClaytonFarr/ralph-playbook/blob/8f58cace8a8e4f4fbbf74b09653b500a2b7f4d6e/README.md, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/workflows/ralph-loop/entry.yaml)

## Hooks

- [Local desktop attention alerts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/hooks/desktop-attention/HOOK.md): Sends a fixed local desktop notification when Claude Code needs permission, input, or an MCP answer, without forwarding prompts or tool contents. Use when: You switch applications while agents work and miss permission or input prompts. — id `desktop-attention`, 7.9/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts claude-code, tags dev-ux, notifications, attention, adapted from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#get-notified-when-claude-needs-input, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/hooks/desktop-attention/entry.yaml)
- [Format after agent edits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/hooks/format-after-edit/HOOK.md): A PostToolUse formatter for explicit edited paths in Claude Code and Codex, including newly added apply_patch files. Uses argument arrays instead of whitespace-splitting xargs and avoids unrelated dirty files. Use when: The project has a formatter, and agents leave style drift or spend turns fixing formatting. — id `format-after-edit`, 7.5/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts claude-code/codex, tags formatting, post-tool-use, adapted from https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/hooks/format-after-edit/entry.yaml)

## Subagents

- [Code reviewer with confidence filtering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/subagents/pr-review-code-reviewer/AGENT.md): A review subagent that checks the current diff against the project's written rules and for real bugs. It scores each issue from 0 to 100 and reports only those at 80 or above, with the file, line, and a fix. ## Custom

Bespoke house items written for this catalog rather than selected from outside research. Recommend them like any other entry when they fit, and say that they are custom.

- [Improvement loop (house prompt)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/skills/improvement-loop/SKILL.md): An explicitly invoked end-of-work loop. It gathers concrete stumbling blocks blamelessly, traces each to a root cause, writes prioritized improvement items with a done-when check, agrees on a short plan with the user, then improves the project's tooling in small reversible steps and verifies each change against the original stumbling block. Use when: You want a deliberate, plan-first improvement pass after a piece of work, ending in tooling changes you approve and can verify. — id `improvement-loop`, type skill, 7.8/10 (human-v1), evidence reviewed, hosts any, tags self-improvement, retrospective, root-cause, tooling, planning, original, [metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/entries/skills/improvement-loop/entry.yaml)

## Collections

- [Debugging](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/collections/debugging.yaml): Diagnose and fix defects with a reproduction-first skill and a rule to verify where the change shows up. Entries: systematic-debugging, verification-evidence
- [Frontend quality](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/collections/frontend-quality.yaml): Improve React and Next.js interfaces with performance guidance, browser verification, evidence-grounded UX critique and final checks. Use native browser tools when sufficient, preserve linked skill prerequisites, and select matching stack guidance for non-React projects. Entries: react-best-practices, webapp-testing, ux-critique, verification-before-completion
- [Open-source maintenance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/collections/open-source-maintenance.yaml): Keep a public repository healthy - audit its documentation, licensing, contributor and release practices, review its workflows, and keep a reviewable commit history. Add open-sourcing only before taking a private repository public. Entries: oss-repo-health, github-actions-hardening, commit-history-hygiene, git-commit, open-sourcing
- [Lightweight project initialization](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/collections/project-initialization.yaml): Research an existing repo or new project's foundation, clarify the goal, write lean project instructions, then implement and verify a runnable first slice. Optional domain modeling, handoff, documentation tools and hooks are selected separately when needed. Entries: repo-research, grilling, agents-md-authoring, explore-plan-implement-review, verification-before-completion
- [Project upkeep](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/collections/project-upkeep.yaml): Turn session retrospectives into project guidance that loads when needed, together with the verification rule. Entries: retrospective, verification-evidence
- [Focused security review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/collections/security-review.yaml): Select a repository threat model, credential serialization review or known-bug variant analysis for the security question at hand. The methods are conditional, not three mandatory scans for every change; variant analysis requires a seed defect. Entries: security-threat-model, secret-serialization, variant-analysis
- [Self-improvement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/collections/self-improvement.yaml): Learn from each session and write the lessons back where they take effect, while keeping always-loaded instructions short. Entries: self-improvement-loop, retrospective, agents-md-authoring, format-after-edit
- [Starter set](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-red/agentic-catalog/main/collections/starter.yaml): A small, portable baseline for most software projects. It covers verification before claiming success, hard-bug diagnosis, stress-testing a plan, and lean project instructions. Entries: verification-before-completion, diagnosing-bugs, grilling, agents-md-authoring, verification-evidence
